stem: Photosynthesis occurs in-
expl: The biochemical process of photosynthesis occurs in the cell organelle called the chloroplast. The green pigment chlorophyll is found in the chloroplast.

stem: The by-product of photosynthesis is :

The overall process of photosynthesis can be represented by the following reaction— Light 6CO+12HO CH O + 6HO + 6O 2 2 Chlorophyll 6 12 6 2 2

expl: The dark reaction of photosynthesis is also called the Blackman reaction. This reaction takes place in the stroma of the chloroplast because enzymes present there reduce CO from the atmosphere and convert it into sugar. 2

stem: Solar energy is converted into ATP in :

options.label: e
options.text: None of the above/More than one of the above

expl: In the chloroplast, solar energy is converted into ATP. The chloroplast is a plant cell organelle in which a protein-containing complex chemical compound called chlorophyll is found. This pigment is responsible for the green colour of leaves.

stem: Which of the following statements is true for the breathing process?

options.label: b
options.text: Energy is released and stored as ATP

options.label: c
options.text: Energy is released and stored as ADP.

options.label: d
options.text: More than one of the above

expl: In the process of respiration, energy is released and stored in the form of ATP. In living cells, the process by which energy is produced as a result of oxidation of food is called cellular respiration. During this process, the released energy is stored in the biomolecule ATP.

stem: Plants appear to bend towards light due to–

options.label: a
options.text: Concentration of auxins at shoot tip

options.label: b
options.text: Concentration of auxins at root tip

options.label: c
options.text: Diffusion of auxins towards the shady side of the shoot

options.label: d
options.text: More than one of the above

expl: Auxins are synthesized at the tip of the shoot and help cells to elongate for a longer time. When light falls on the plant from one side, auxin diffuses towards the shaded side of the shoot. The higher auxin concentration on the shaded side stimulates the cells there to elongate more (i.e., on the side away from light). Therefore, the plant appears to bend towards the light.

stem: Water passes from the soil into the root by the physical process is called -

options.label: e
options.text: None of the above/More than one of the above

expl: Water reaches the roots from the soil through the process of osmosis.

stem: Photosynthesis occurs—

options.label: b
options.text: During the day and at night

options.label: c
options.text: During the day or at night

expl: Photosynthesis is a process in green plants in which they prepare food. In this process, light provides the energy. Naturally, plants obtain energy from sunlight, but marine algae can perform this process in moonlight, and photosynthesis can also occur in plants under electric light.

stem: The process by which plants produce food is called :
expl: Photosynthesis is a process in green plants in which they prepare food. In this process, light provides the energy. Naturally, plants obtain energy from sunlight, but marine algae can perform this process in moonlight, and photosynthesis can also occur in plants under electric light.

stem: Where does photosynthesis take place in the cells of a leaf?
expl: The process of photosynthesis occurs in all chloroplast-containing cells of the plant, i.e., in all green parts of the plant. This process occurs especially in the mesophyll tissue of leaves.

stem: Which of the following the chlorophyll in photosynthesis is used for ?
expl: Photosynthesis is the process by which green plants, in the presence of sunlight, form carbohydrates by the combination of water and carbon dioxide. In this process, oxygen is released as a by-product. Chlorophyll is a chemical photoreceptor (light-absorbing pigment) that captures light for photosynthesis in plants. It absorbs light mainly in the red (long wavelength) and blue (short wavelength) regions of the visible spectrum. Absorption of green light is very low, and the green light is reflected. That is why a plant appears green.

stem: Chlorophyll absorbs ______ wavelengths of the sunlight.

options.label: d
options.text: More than one of the above

expl: Chlorophyll is a photoreceptor (light-sensitive) chemical that absorbs light for photosynthesis in plants. It absorbs visible light mainly in the red (long-wavelength) and blue (short-wavelength) regions. Absorption of green light is very low, and green light is reflected. That is why plants appear green.

stem: The process of breaking down organic matter by micro organisms is called :
expl: Decomposers are those biotic components that, for their nutrition, decompose the dead bodies (organic matter) of producers and consumers. These mainly include microorganisms (especially bacteria and fungi). As a result of this process, complex organic substances are decomposed into simpler organic substance such as carbon dioxide, water and mineral nutrients (e.g. nitrate, phosphates, calciumetc.

stem: Which of the following is a plant hormone?

options.label: d
options.text: More than one of the above

expl: Plant hormones, also called phytohormones, are chemicals that regulate plant growth. Mainly five hormones are found in plants—auxin, gibberellin, cytokinin, ethylene, and abscisic acid.

stem: Which of the following plants has modified its stem to store food material?

options.label: e
options.text: None of the above/More than one of the above

expl: Plants such as turmeric, ginger, and potato store food material in modified stems, whereas radish, carrot, beetroot, turnip, sweet potato, etc. are modifications of roots.

stem: Water is conducted in vascular plants by-
expl: Water and mineral nutrients absorbed by roots are carried throughout the plant by the conducting tissue called xylem, whereas phloem transports food.

stem: Which pigment is essential for nitrogen fixation by leguminous plants?

options.label: d
options.text: More than one of the above

expl: Leghemoglobin is an important pigment for nitrogen fixation in leguminous plants. It protects the nitrogen-fixation enzyme system from oxygen, which is harmful to it.

stem: The most important part of the plant in terms of its life cycle is–
expl: From the life-cycle point of view, the flower is the most important part of the plant. In the flower, the embryo develops through pollination, which forms the seed. On germination of the seed, a new plant is formed again.

stem: Pea plant is :
expl: Pea is a dicotyledonous herbaceous plant. It is a rabi crop. Swarna Rekha, Aparna, Paras, Ambika, etc. are its main varieties.

stem: legumes are highly nutritious because they are rich in:

options.label: e
options.text: None of the above/More than one of the above

expl: Pulses contain a large amount of protein. Their plants belong to the family Leguminosae/Fabaceae. Their root nodules contain bacteria that fix nitrogen. Examples—pea, pigeon pea (arhar), green gram (moong), soybean, groundnut, black gram (urad), etc.

stem: Xylem in plants is responsible for following function:

options.label: b
options.text: Transport of water and dissolved minerals

options.label: c
options.text: Transport of oxygen and other gases

expl: Xylem is one of the vascular (conducting) tissues of vascular plants. Its main function is to carry the water and dissolved mineral salts absorbed by the roots to the stem, leaves, and other parts of the plant. This transport generally occurs from bottom to top (from root to leaf), so it is considered unidirectional transport.

stem: . The stomata open or close due to changes in the

options.label: d
options.text: More than one of the above

expl: During the day, due to higher transpiration, water is absorbed by the roots and transported to different parts of the plant through xylem, due to which the guard cells become swollen (turgid). As a result, the stomata open. At night, the guard cells shrink and become rigid because the roots absorb less water; therefore, the stomata close. Potassium plays an important role in the opening and closing of stomata.

stem: Which of the following is not a correct match?

options.label: b
options.text: Thick, hard stem with branching near the base: Tree

options.label: c
options.text: Weak stem which cannot stand upright: Creeper

options.label: d
options.text: More than one of the above

expl: A plant with a thick, hard stem and branches near the base is not a tree; it is a shrub. Note that plants play the role of major producers on Earth. Also, plants are known by different names in different forms: the petiole connects the leaf to the stem, and a creeper (vine) is a type of weak stem that cannot stand upright without support.

stem: The stem of the plant helps in distributing food to all parts of the plant. it also helps in -

options.label: e
options.text: None of the above / more than one of the above

expl: The stem helps in distributing food (nutrients) along with water to all parts of the plant and also in storing food (nutrients). It supports the leaves, flowers, and fruits and plays a major role in giving shape to the plant as well.

stem: Water reaches great heights in trees because of suction pull caused by

options.label: d
options.text: More than one of the above

expl: Transpiration is a process in which loss of water vapour occurs through the stomata of (mainly leaves). The loss of water vapour from the plant cools the plant when the weather is very hot.

stem: The part which we eat in Mango is :
expl: From a botanical point of view, mango is a single-seeded fleshy fruit (Drupe). In such fruits, the pericarp is divided into three parts— 1. Exocarp/Epicarp – the peel of the mango. 2. Mesocarp – the fleshy pulp that we eat. 3. Endocarp – the inner hard layer, seen as the hard stone in mango.

stem: The edible part of litchi is -

options.label: d
options.text: More than one of the above

expl: Litchi is a tasty, juicy subtropical fruit. The edible part of litchi is the aril. Botanically, litchi belongs to the family Sapindaceae. In India, the highest production of litchi is in Bihar.

stem: Ginger is a stem, not a root, because-

options.label: c
options.text: It grows horizontally in the soil.

options.label: e
options.text: None of the above/More than one of the above

expl: Ginger (botanical name: Zingiber officinale) is a modified underground stem, not a root, because it has nodes and internodes. It is a rhizome, i.e., an underground modification of the stem. A rhizome is a branched, prostrate, horizontally growing stem. Other examples of rhizomes are turmeric, banana, and fern.

stem: Ginger is an underground stem and not a root because

options.label: d
options.text: More than one of the above

expl: Ginger (botanical name: Zingiber officinale) is a modified underground stem, not a root, because it has nodes and internodes. It is a rhizome, i.e., an underground modification of the stem. A rhizome is a branched, prostrate, horizontally growing stem. Other examples of rhizomes are turmeric, banana, and fern.

stem: Water enters from soil into root hairs of plants due to

options.label: d
options.text: More than one of the above

expl: In plants, the basic process of water absorption occurs through root hairs. These root hairs remain in contact with soil particles, and the cells absorb water due to osmotic pressure. Each root hair has a vacuole filled with cell sap.

stem: What is the movement of the leaves of the sensitive plant Mimosa pudica called?
expl: The movement of leaves of the sensitive plant Mimosa pudica is called seismonasty (a response to touch/shock). It is a feature found in some plants, in which responce occurs when the plant is touched or shaken in any way.

stem: Which one of the following is a vegetative hormone?

options.label: d
options.text: More than one of the above

expl: Cytokinin is a plant hormone. Plant hormones control the development, growth, and reproductive processes of plants. Insulin is an animal hormone (a peptide/protein hormone). Estrogen is a group of hormones that plays an important role in normal sexual and reproductive development in women.

stem: Plants are formed like parent plant from –
expl: Vegetative propagation is an asexual method of reproduction. In this method, new plants are obtained from parts of old plants (such as stem, root, and leaves) without the involvement of reproductive organs. Stem cutting, layering, and grafting are common methods. New plants produced by asexual reproduction are morphologically and genetically similar to their parent. In contrast, plants produced by sexual reproduction (from seeds) show variations.

stem: Embryo is found in –
expl: In plants, the embryo is found in the seed. As a result of the germination process, the embryo comes out of the seed.

stem: Water-pollinated flowers have pollen grains that are:

options.label: d
options.text: More than one of the above

expl: In water-pollinated flowers, pollen grains are dry.

stem: Stem cutting is done generally to grow –
expl: Vegetative propagation of sugarcane is done by stem cuttings (called setts) or by ratooning. However, with each ratoon crop, the yield keeps decreasing after every 3–4 years, fresh stem cuttings with buds have to be replanted.

stem: Among the following, which is not a true fruit?

options.label: e
options.text: None of the above / More than one of the above

expl: If, in the formation of a fruit, some parts other than the ovary are also involved, such a fruit is called a false fruit. Examples— apple, cashew nut, pear, pineapple, strawberry, etc.

stem: Buds are specifically found—

options.label: a
options.text: At the base (axil) of leaves and at the ends of branches

expl: Buds are specifically found in the axils of leaves and at the ends of branches (at both ends, as stated). The development of buds on leaves indicates the process of growth and maturity in plants.

stem: The part of the flower that gives rise to a fruit is

options.label: e
options.text: None of the above / More than one of the above

expl: A flower is the reproductive organ of a plant. In a flower, calyx, corolla, androecium and gynoecium are present. The androecium is the male reproductive part, while the gynoecium is the female reproductive part. In the gynoecium, the pistil is present, which has three parts— ovary, style and stigma. Later, the ovary of the flower develops and takes the form of a fruit.

stem: Pollination is best defined as –

options.label: a
options.text: transfer of pollen grains from anther to stigma

options.label: c
options.text: growth of pollen tube in ovule

options.label: e
options.text: None of the above/More than one of the above

expl: In scientific terms, pollination is the process in which pollen grains are transferred from anther to the stigma. After fertilization, the ovary develops into a fruit and the ovules develops into seeds.

stem: A plant bud is –
expl: In botany, an undeveloped shoot (embryonic shoot) is called a bud or budlet. It arises either in the axil of a leaf or at the terminal end of the stem.

stem: Clove, a spice, is obtained from which part of the plant?

options.label: e
options.text: None of the above/More than one of the above

expl: Cloves are dried flower buds, used in food items, as a pain reliever, etc. The botanical name of clove is Syzygium aromaticum, which belongs to the family Myrtaceae. Indonesia is considered its place of origin, and it is used throughout the world. It is an evergreen tree, about 10–20 meters tall, and its leaves are large and oval.

Indonesia is considered its place of origin, and it is used throughout the world. It is an evergreen tree, about 10–20 meters tall, and its leaves are large and oval.

stem: Turmeric powder is obtained from which part of the turmeric plant ?
expl: Turmeric powder is obtained from the underground stem of the turmeric plant, i.e., the rhizome. After cutting the rhizome and removing the outer layer, the remaining part is dried and ground to make turmeric powder.

stem: What is the scientific name of the spice 'Curcuma lon-ga'?
expl: ‘Curcuma longa’ is the scientific name of turmeric. The scientific name of cumin is Cuminum cyminum, the scientific name of clove is Syzygium aromaticum, and the scientific name of coriander is Coriandrum sativum.

stem: Pine, Fir, Spruce, Cedar, larch and Cypress are the famous timber-yielding plants of which several also occur widely in the hilly regions of india. All these belong to –

options.label: e
options.text: None of the above/More than one of the above

expl: Pine, fir, spruce, cedar, larch and cypress are well-known timber-yielding plants. They are coniferous trees found in mountain forests. All of these are gymnosperms.

stem: insulin is received from -
expl: Inulin is a polysaccharide. It is found in the roots of dahlia, onion, garlic, banana, and shatavari (Asparagus).

stem: Quinine is a common drug for malaria that is obtained from a plant. Which part of the plant yields this drug?
expl: Quinine is an important medicine for the treatment of malaria. It is obtained from the bark of the Cinchona plant. This plant is an angiospermic. Quinine is a natural white crystalline alkaloid with a bitter taste. It is also used in the treatment of nocturnal leg cramps.

stem: Where does aspirin come from?
expl: Aspirin and antipyretic (fever-reducing) medicines act as pain relievers. They are obtained from the bark of the willow tree.

stem: Aspirin is -
expl: Aspirin is an antipyretic.

stem: Which one of the following is not an antibiotic?

options.label: e
options.text: None of the above/More than one of the above

expl: Oxytocin is a hormone found in mammals. It is produced in a part of the brain called the hypothalamus and is secreted by the pituitary gland. It has a special role in bonding and social attachment ; therefore, it is also called the “love hormone”, whereas erythromycin and penicillin, etc. are examples of antibiotics.

stem: Which one of the following is an antibiotic drug?

options.label: e
options.text: None of the above/More than one of the above

expl: Chloramphenicol is an antibiotic medicine used for the treatment of bacterial infections. Sulfaguanidine is a type of sulfonamide antibiotic, which works as an antibacterial agent. Thus, more than one option is correct for this question.

stem: Which of the following is an antibiotic?

options.label: e
options.text: None of the above/More than one of the above

expl: Among the above options, penicillin and sulfadiazine are antibiotics. Antibiotics are used for the treatment of diseases caused by bacteria. Therefore, the correct answer is option (e).

stem: An example of an antibiotic drug is -

options.label: e
options.text: None of the above/More than one of the above

expl: Among the above options, penicillin and sulfadiazine are antibiotics. Antibiotics are used for the treatment of diseases caused by bacteria. Therefore, the correct answer is option (e).

stem: The longest living tree is-
expl: The tallest/highest tree is the coastal redwood (Sequoia sempervirens) or Hyperion, whose height, according to Guinness World Records, is about 116.07 metres.

stem: Which of the food grains is richest in protein?
expl: Among plant foods, soybean has the maximum protein content. Its protein content is approximately 38–42%, which is higher than other pulses.

stem: The largest flower in the world is-
expl: The world’s largest flower is Rafflesia arnoldii. It was first discovered by Joseph Arnold in 1818. The weight of this flower can be up to about 7-11 kg.
